questions.article: Ungodly Activities in the Name of God
questions.q: After the Paris attacks, what example from Japan does the editorial offer to show how a people can be turned from violence?
options: Japan replaced its language and customs
Not quite. The article says: After the war, educated Japanese spread peaceful ideas through writing and speech until the national mindset changed.
Japan punished every former soldier
Not quite. The article says: After the war, educated Japanese spread peaceful ideas through writing and speech until the national mindset changed.
After the war, educated Japanese spread peaceful ideas through writing and speech until the national mindset changed
Yes. Minds were re-engineered, not forced.
Japan closed its borders for a generation
Not quite. The article says: After the war, educated Japanese spread peaceful ideas through writing and speech until the national mindset changed.
questions.rationale: “This miracle occurred by way of dissemination of peaceful ideas through literature and several public speeches and broadcasts.”

questions.article: Ungodly Activities in the Name of God
questions.q: By what, according to the editorial, should Islam be judged?
options: By the laws of Muslim countries
Not quite. The article says: By its scripture, not by the acts of those who claim it.
By its scripture, not by the acts of those who claim it
Right. The Quran likens killing one person to killing all mankind.
By reports in the press
Not quite. The article says: By its scripture, not by the acts of those who claim it.
By the conduct of the majority
Not quite. The article says: By its scripture, not by the acts of those who claim it.
questions.rationale: “Islam should be judged through its scripture and not through the practice of Muslims.”

questions.q: Why, according to the article, do people fail to accept a truth they could recognise?
options: Truth changes from age to age
Not quite. The article says: Psychological barriers – it may upset their way of life, lower their standing, or come from someone they look down on.
The truth is too hard to understand
Not quite. The article says: Psychological barriers – it may upset their way of life, lower their standing, or come from someone they look down on.
They have not been told it often enough
Not quite. The article says: Psychological barriers – it may upset their way of life, lower their standing, or come from someone they look down on.
Psychological barriers – it may upset their way of life, lower their standing, or come from someone they look down on
Yes. Honest thought would have led them to accept it.
questions.rationale: “They are psychologically inhibited from doing so. Acceptance of the truth might disrupt their materialistic life-pattern. They might have to lower their worldly status.”

questions.q: What method of lasting change does the article recommend, citing the Fabian Society?
options: Mass rallies and slogans
Not quite. The article says: Patiently shaping individual minds and forming a small committed team; crowds do not build.
Patiently shaping individual minds and forming a small committed team; crowds do not build
Well read. One sincere person outweighs a thousand half-hearted ones.
Waiting for a great leader
Not quite. The article says: Patiently shaping individual minds and forming a small committed team; crowds do not build.
Seizing power first
Not quite. The article says: Patiently shaping individual minds and forming a small committed team; crowds do not build.
questions.rationale: “Whatever one wants to accomplish at a mass level, one has to adopt the method of addressing individual minds.”

questions.q: An elderly scholar gave his daughter and son-in-law his life’s savings in place of a lavish wedding. What is the article’s point?
options: A wedding is the start of serious responsibility; money is better spent helping the couple begin than on display
Correct. They built a business with it.
Weddings should not be celebrated at all
Not quite. The article says: A wedding is the start of serious responsibility; money is better spent helping the couple begin than on display.
Parents owe their children a fortune
Not quite. The article says: A wedding is the start of serious responsibility; money is better spent helping the couple begin than on display.
Scholars are usually poor
Not quite. The article says: A wedding is the start of serious responsibility; money is better spent helping the couple begin than on display.
questions.rationale: “One’s wedding is a very serious event in life, not just an occasion for senseless showing off… would it not be better to avoid ostentation altogether and to think of how best one can help the young couple?”

questions.q: What does the article advise someone who has no financial need to work?
options: To leave work to those who need it
Not quite. The article says: To turn to higher aims and worthy causes and keep fruitfully occupied.
To travel until an interest appears
Not quite. The article says: To turn to higher aims and worthy causes and keep fruitfully occupied.
To enjoy well-earned leisure
Not quite. The article says: To turn to higher aims and worthy causes and keep fruitfully occupied.
To turn to higher aims and worthy causes and keep fruitfully occupied
Yes. Idleness is called a poison.
questions.rationale: “If one is financially independent, one should turn one’s attention to higher things, pursue noble ends, serve worthy causes and keep oneself fruitfully occupied.”

questions.q: What does the article name as “the price of heaven”?
options: Gratitude – a thankful heart that rises above life’s difficulties
Right. No one can be completely happy here.
Long years of solitude
Not quite. The article says: Gratitude – a thankful heart that rises above life’s difficulties.
Great wealth given away
Not quite. The article says: Gratitude – a thankful heart that rises above life’s difficulties.
A trouble-free life
Not quite. The article says: Gratitude – a thankful heart that rises above life’s difficulties.

questions.article: Don’t Be a Slave to Your Desires
questions.q: To what does the article liken desire in the working of a person’s life?
options: The fuel, without which nothing moves
Not quite. The article says: Grease for the engine, not its driver.
The road, which decides the destination
Not quite. The article says: Grease for the engine, not its driver.
Grease for the engine, not its driver
Yes. It may motivate, but reason must steer.
The brakes, which stop every journey
Not quite. The article says: Grease for the engine, not its driver.
questions.rationale: “It is like grease to an engine and not like the driver of that engine… Never judge a desire for its own sake—always judge it in terms of the results of its fulfilment.”

questions.q: Besides reward in the Hereafter, what benefit of patience in this life does the article describe?
options: It makes others give way
Not quite. The article says: It saves one from despair and gives the steadiness to plan with confidence.
It brings quick results
Not quite. The article says: It saves one from despair and gives the steadiness to plan with confidence.
It saves one from despair and gives the steadiness to plan with confidence
Well read. It keeps conviction firm.
It removes all difficulties
Not quite. The article says: It saves one from despair and gives the steadiness to plan with confidence.
questions.rationale: “Patience helps save you from despair… He lives with a strong sense of certainty. He is able to courageously plan the course of his life.”

questions.q: Commenting on plans to make Mars habitable, what does the article say man should work towards?
options: Cities under the sea
Not quite. The article says: Paradise, the future abode in God’s plan – and a change in his own thinking.
A longer human lifespan
Not quite. The article says: Paradise, the future abode in God’s plan – and a change in his own thinking.
A colony on the moon
Not quite. The article says: Paradise, the future abode in God’s plan – and a change in his own thinking.
Paradise, the future abode in God’s plan – and a change in his own thinking
Yes. If such technology existed, it should first restore the earth.
questions.rationale: “The time has come for man to transform his thinking and work towards attaining Paradise, which according to the creation plan of God will be man’s future abode.”
